title: Capacity reservation and graceful fallback — architecture review notes
content:
Meeting: Architecture review — capacity reservation + graceful fallback for multi-region Dedicated pools
Date: 2025-02-11 10:00–11:30 PT
Attendees: Priya Shah (chair), Marco Alvarez, Leah Kim, Jonah Price, Aisha Rahman, Tim O. (SRE consult), + notes from offline: Mei L. (cost analytics)
Goal: Decide an approach for reserving dedicated capacity per-customer/tenant across regions, define fallback rules when reserved capacity is exhausted, and capture telemetry + rollout plan.

Agenda:
- Quick problem statement and constraints (5m)
- Present proposals (30m)
- Tradeoffs, SLA impact, cost modelling (20m)
- Failure modes + safety nets (15m)
- Rollout plan + telemetry + action items (20m)

Summary (TL;DR):
We agreed to pursue a hybrid reservation model (Proposal C) that stitches short-duration regional reservations with a global soft-pool fallback. Core idea: maintain a committed per-tenant regional reservation for steady baseline throughput and a globally routable shared pool for burst workloads; fallback to lower-tier model variants or queueing when both are saturated. This balances predictability (for enterprise SLAs) and better overall utilization.

Problem statement, restated in-brief:
- Customers on Dedicated want consistent p99 latency and throughput guarantees across regions for critical routes.
- Capacity is expensive; naive per-tenant pinned pools underutilize GPUs when traffic is spiky and regionally imbalanced.
- Need clear failure and degradation semantics for apps when reserved capacity is unavailable (esp. during regional outages).
- Must preserve security/isolation requirements (no data crossing without encryption and audit trail).

Constraints:
- Must work with existing Dedicated autoscaler and tenant slot scheduler (no major runtime rewrite).
- Need pluggable routing policy so product can expose "strict SLA" vs "best-effort" flags for routes.
- Cost impact target: incremental increase < 8% on average cluster utilization vs current baseline (aim for improvement, not regression).
- Rollout must support canary and per-customer opt-in.

Proposals considered:
A) Strict per-tenant regional reservation: each tenant gets pinned capacity in region(s) they request. Simple semantics, but high waste and hard to handle cross-region failover.
B) Global reserved bucket + soft regional allocation: reservation at the global level with weighted regional assignment, fallback routes traffic to other regions if needed. Pros: better utilization; Cons: network egress/security, cross-region latency.
C) Hybrid: short-duration regional reservations (baseline pinned slots sized to steady-state traffic) + global shared soft-pool for bursts; fallback policy to lower-cost model variants / queue + automatic canary-based model swap. (Chosen)

Why we chose C (architectural rationale):
- Lower cold waste: baseline regional pins sized by 95th percentile steady usage (slack window) — reduces overcommit risk vs long-term pins.
- Bursts routed to shared soft-pool to utilize idle GPUs across tenants; avoids cross-tenant noisy-neighbor if bounded by preemptible tier and lower SLO.
- Clear degradation ladder for operators and product: baseline (reserved) -> soft-pool -> lower-tier model -> queue/failure with controlled error codes and client hints.
- Works with existing runtime slot allocator: add a reservation lease + global soft-pool allocator service.

Key components required:
- Reservation lease manager (Platform service): issues short-duration regional leases per tenant (TTL ~ 5–15m, renews automatically), exposes diagnostics (owner, token, capacity counts).
- Global soft-pool scheduler: arbitrates preemptible slots, enforces per-tenant burst budget and preemption policies.
- Routing policy switch: route decisions consider tenant reservation state, route policy & region preference, and model tier.
- Fallback matrix (configurable per-tenant/route): ordered list of fallbacks with SLA cost multipliers and client-facing error codes.
- Telemetry: per-request tags (reservation_hit, softpool_hit, preempted, fallback_reason), latency and cost counters.

SLA and billing implications:
- Reserved capacity remains billable at current committed rates. Soft-pool usage billed at burst rate (higher unit cost).
- Fallback to lower-tier models reduces per-token cost; need billing product changes to show fallback-premium and soft-pool premiums.
- SLA contract language: product to define "Reserved throughput" guarantees; fallbacks will be reflected in reduced SLA credit if lower-tier used. Product will work with legal on phrasing.

Failure modes and mitigations:
1) Lease manager partition / failure -> risk: reservations not renewed -> mass fallbacks.
   - Mitigation: local read-through cache on node (cached reservation until TTL+delta), leader election for small lease quorum, circuit-breaker to keep existing reservations for 30s if manager unreachable.
2) Soft-pool noisy neighbor -> risk: tenant bursts hog soft-pool.
   - Mitigation: per-tenant burst caps, weighted fair sharing, token-bucket with backpressure, enforce preemption window and minimum reserved capacity.
3) Cross-region routing increases tail latency during failover.
   - Mitigation: only route cross-region when soft-pool cannot satisfy within region, otherwise route to lower-tier local models; expose client hints for degraded latency.
4) Billing inconsistency (billing lag) -> customer surprise.
   - Mitigation: instrumentation and billing preview dashboard before GA; grace period for initial customers.

Operational plan and telemetry:
- Telemetry: add reservation_hit (bool), reservation_age_ms, softpool_latency_ms, fallback_reason (enum), preempted_by (tenant_id or system). Emit per-request and aggregate daily dashboards.
- Alerts: reservation-manager error rate > 1% -> P1. Soft-pool saturation > 90% for > 5m -> P1. Preemption churn > threshold -> P2.
- SLO experiments: run canary customers with SLA flag; monitor p50/p95/p99 and error profiles for 72h before wider rollout.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Spike: implement reservation manager (service) + soft-pool scheduler prototypes; test on staging with synthetic multi-region traffic. (2–3 weeks)
2) Canary: enable for 2 low-risk tenants (opt-in) with product team present; monitor. (1 month)
3) Expand to small cohort (10 tenants) and refine configs. (1 month)
4) Gradual GA with product + legal updates, billing preview, docs, and console controls. (quarterly alignment)

Telemetry and testing checklist (owner initials):
- Add per-request tags + aggregate dashboards (Jonah) — due 2025-02-20
- Load test scenarios (regional spike, cross-region failover) (Leah) — due 2025-02-25
- Cost model run with Mei (offline) — due 2025-02-18
- Billing preview in console (product + billing) — Priya / Product ops — due 2025-03-05

Open questions (needs follow-up):
- Reservation TTL value tradeoffs: 5m vs 15m vs 60m — what renew failure semantics are acceptable? (SRE input)
- Backpressure behavior for SDKs — should SDKs expose retry hints or do we surface via response headers? (developer-experience)
- Regulatory requirements for cross-region routing for specific customers — need security/legal checklist for opt-in.
- Preemption fairness: algorithm details: token-bucket + priority queue vs weighted fair share? (deeper design task)

Action items (concrete):
- Marco: PR skeleton for reservation-manager prototype (repo & interface spec) — due 2025-02-17
- Leah: define load-test harness and initial scenarios commit — due 2025-02-25
- Jonah: dashboards + alert playbook (first draft) — due 2025-02-20
- Aisha: draft product billing and console changes for soft-pool visibility — due 2025-02-28
- Priya: coordinate legal wording for SLA and cross-region fallback (sync with legal) — due 2025-03-03

Notes to self / miscellaneous scribbles:
- consider reserving vGPU fractions for small tenants to avoid 1:1 GPU pinned waste
- early export: "reservation_hit" counter will be useful for product to show utilization per-tenant
- check compatibility with Dedicated autoscaler fast-path (avoid double-scheduling)

Referenced docs / offline links:
- RFC-PE-22 (reservation + fallback) — draft in Confluence (CONFLUENCE-PE-RESERVE-FB-RFC)
- JIRA-PE-789 (implementation epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/456 (prototype allocator)

Decisions recorded:
- Pick Proposal C (hybrid) for next-stage implementation work.
- Use short TTL reservation leases, add local node cache to tolerate controller flakiness.
- Billing: soft-pool billed at premium; reserved capacity is committed billing. Product to finalize wording.

Next meeting: follow-up design check-in, 2025-02-18 11:00 PT — focus on reservation-manager API and load-test plan.

End of notes.
